rooms.label: Section Office, Whitehall
rooms.description: The same office. Rain against the same sash windows. Alderton is at his desk, a street plan of the fourth district open in front of him — the consulate building circled in red ink. He closes the folder when Jacob enters.

examineTargets.label: Alderton
examineTargets.description: He speaks without looking up from the plan. 'Kuznetsov. First Secretary, Cultural Section. Bad hip — a road accident, Minsk, three years ago. He can walk, but not fast, and not stairs without support. He's agreed to come. He's been waiting.' He picks up his pen. 'You need to be out of the building before the duty officer rotation at eleven. The car will be on the side street. Grey Peugeot. Driver knows the route.' He doesn't wait for questions.

examineTargets.label: the street plan
examineTargets.description: A 1:200 scale plan of the building and surrounding block. The consulate occupies the ground and first floors of a four-storey building on Neustiftgasse. A pencilled cross marks a ground-floor window: the kitchen. Another marks the side alley. A third marks Kuznetsov's room: fourteen, first floor.

examineTargets.label: the window
examineTargets.description: London in the rain. A bus. A man walking fast with his collar up. None of them know you exist. In forty-eight hours you'll be glad of that.

rooms.label: Neustiftgasse
rooms.description: A respectable street in the fourth district — wide pavements, grey stone, the yellow stucco of the consulate building ahead. A lamp post casts a yellow oval on the wet cobbles. The consulate entrance is thirty metres ahead, lit by a single exterior lamp. The side alley is to your left.

addenda.text: A light has come on in an upper window. Someone inside is moving fast.

exits.label: Cross the forecourt to the consulate entrance

examineTargets.label: the consulate building
examineTargets.description: Four storeys of grey stone, Soviet flag over the entrance. Most of the windows are dark. On the ground floor, left side, a light is on — the kitchen. The side alley runs along the right of the building and looks unlit.

examineTargets.label: the guard
examineTargets.description: A broad man in a dark coat, moving slowly along the pavement, then back. He has a smoke at the corner of the alley, then moves again. His name is Baranov. He has been doing this for two hours and does not look like a man who minds.

examineTargets.label: the kitchen light
examineTargets.description: The ground-floor window on the left side of the building — warm light, the silhouette of someone at a worktop. When it goes off, the kitchen staff will have finished for the night. The service entrance will be unattended except for the night watch.

rooms.label: Side Alley
rooms.description: A narrow alley between the consulate and the building next door. Dustbins, a drainpipe, the smell of wet brick. A grey Peugeot is parked where the alley meets the far street, engine off, driver in his seat.

addenda.text: The Peugeot's engine turns over quietly. The driver has seen you.

exits.label: Down the alley to the service yard

examineTargets.label: the grey Peugeot
examineTargets.description: A 1961 Peugeot 404, grey, Austrian plates. The driver is in his seat, hat forward, not watching you. He knows you're here.

examineTargets.label: the service door
examineTargets.description: A steel door at the base of the building, set flush with the wall. No handle on this side. It opens outward from the basement storeroom when unlatched from inside.

examineTargets.label: the drain cover
examineTargets.description: A cast-iron drain cover, loose in its housing. The kind of loose that suggests someone was here before you.

rooms.label: Consulate Entrance Hall
rooms.description: A panelled entrance hall, red carpet worn to grey in the centre, the Soviet coat of arms on the wall behind a reception desk. A young woman in a grey suit sits at the desk, a telephone beside her and a visitor's register open in front of her. The corridor beyond requires a signature.

addenda.text: Baranov is at the entrance, coat open, hand near his sidearm, watching the door.
Your name is in the register.

examineTargets.label: the receptionist
examineTargets.description: A woman in her thirties, unimpressed. She has been here since eight this morning and has four more hours to go. She picks up a pen.

effect.text: You sign the register. She does not look at the name.

examineTargets.label: the visitor register
examineTargets.description: A hardback ledger. The last entry is from yesterday — a delegation from the East German trade ministry. Three names, a time, a signature that could be anything.

examineTargets.label: the Soviet coat of arms
examineTargets.description: Hammer, sickle, ears of wheat. The varnish is cracking at the bottom left corner.

rooms.label: Service Yard
rooms.description: A narrow yard between the consulate and a blank stone wall. Wooden pallets stacked against the building, a rubbish bin, a drain. The service door stands open — kitchen staff propped it when they took out the bins. No lights.

addenda.text: A door bangs somewhere above. A light has come on in the upper floors.

exits.label: Through the service door into the kitchen

examineTargets.label: the service door
examineTargets.description: A steel door, propped open with a bin. The kitchen beyond is lit and empty. The sound of the fan above the range.

examineTargets.label: the pallets
examineTargets.description: Stacked three high against the building. Nothing underneath. Good cover if you need to wait.

rooms.label: Consulate Kitchen
rooms.description: A working kitchen, larger than expected. Industrial range, stainless worktops, the smell of garlic and cleaning fluid. The evening staff have gone — equipment cooling, lights on. A door on the far wall leads into the consulate corridor. It is locked.

addenda.text: Voices from the corridor beyond the inner door. Someone is running.
The inner door to the corridor stands open.

examineTargets.label: the inner door
examineTargets.description: A wooden door with a standard pin-tumbler lock. Connects the kitchen to the ground-floor corridor. Locked from this side.

effect.text: The lock gives. You ease the door open an inch and listen.

examineTargets.label: the range
examineTargets.description: Still warm. Cabbage, something with dill. Whatever Zima eats for dinner is better than most of what Jacob has eaten this month.

examineTargets.label: the kitchen rota
examineTargets.description: Pinned to the wall near the service door. Zima, M. — night check, 21:00 and 23:00. Tonight he is early.

rooms.label: Ground Floor Corridor
rooms.description: A plastered corridor, strip lighting, numbered doors. The carpet runner is a different shade of red than the entrance hall. Petrov stands near the far end with his weight on one foot, looking at nothing in particular. There is a small key cabinet on the wall beside his post.

addenda.text: Petrov has moved to the corridor entrance, hand on his sidearm.

examineTargets.label: the notice board
examineTargets.description: A duty roster, a memo about the boiler, a printed photograph of the Soviet premier. Petrov's name appears on the night duty list. The rota ends Friday.

examineTargets.label: the stairwell door
examineTargets.description: A fire door with a simple warded lock. Access to the first floor — residential and senior staff quarters. Restricted after hours.

examineTargets.label: the key cabinet
examineTargets.description: A small metal cabinet on the wall near Petrov's post. Locked with a warded lock. A spare for the stairwell, most likely.

effect.text: The cabinet opens. A brass key on a hook.

rooms.label: Duty Officer's Office
rooms.description: A small room at the end of the corridor — a desk, a bookshelf, a filing cabinet. A framed commendation on the wall in Cyrillic. Two chairs facing the desk, angled inward as if waiting for an argument to resume.

addenda.text: The desk chair has been pushed back hard. Petrov left in a hurry.

examineTargets.label: the desk
examineTargets.description: Papers, a cold glass of tea, an ashtray. A list of extension numbers, handwritten. Petrov has added his own notes in the margins — shift times, a name circled twice.

examineTargets.label: the commendation
examineTargets.description: Petrov, V.I. — for service to the ministry. Signed in 1956. Whatever he did, it was eight years ago.

examineTargets.label: the letter on the desk
examineTargets.description: Half-written, in a small careful hand. It begins: 'Mother — the posting has been extended. I do not know when I will be back. The city is fine. The food is not so bad.' It ends there.

rooms.label: Staff Common Room
rooms.description: A low table, four chairs, a kettle on a sideboard. Magazines in Russian, a chess set mid-game on the windowsill. A roster on the wall shows who is on post tonight. The room is empty.

addenda.text: The chess pieces have been knocked to the floor. Someone left in a hurry.

examineTargets.label: the duty roster
examineTargets.description: Tonight's posting. Petrov: ground floor, all night. Baranov: exterior, 20:00 to 00:00. Zima: kitchen and service, 21:00 to 01:00. Volkov: first floor residential, 21:00 to 05:00. A full house.

examineTargets.label: the chess set
examineTargets.description: A problem in progress — white to play, pinned in an unfavourable endgame. Someone has been thinking about this for days.

examineTargets.label: the kettle
examineTargets.description: Warm. Someone was here not long ago. A mug on the sideboard — half a cup of tea, no longer steaming.

rooms.label: Medical Room
rooms.description: A single-bed clinic. Bandages, a first aid cabinet on the wall, the smell of antiseptic. A wheelchair sits in the corner. Irina Molova, the duty nurse, is at a small desk near the window, reading, back to the door.

addenda.text: Irina is gone. The bandages on the desk are untouched, her chair pushed back.

examineTargets.label: Irina Molova
examineTargets.description: The duty nurse. Mid-forties, reading glasses, the expression of someone who has worked night shifts for too long. She has not heard you yet.

examineTargets.label: the first aid cabinet
examineTargets.description: Standard-issue Soviet medical kit. Bandages, iodine, a packet of aspirin. Nothing useful for tonight's work.

examineTargets.label: the patient log
examineTargets.description: Last entry, dated three weeks ago: a guard with a sprained wrist. Before that: Kuznetsov, Y. — referred for physiotherapy, hip. Not attended.

rooms.label: Service Corridor
rooms.description: A narrow back corridor behind the main rooms — pipes, a junction box, the smell of old paint. A single bulb on a wire. Connects to the basement storeroom at the far end.

addenda.text: A distant door banging somewhere in the stairwell. The pipes are cold.

examineTargets.label: the junction box
examineTargets.description: Electrical, clearly original. The building is older than its current use. Someone has added modern wiring alongside the old.

examineTargets.label: the pipes
examineTargets.description: Hot water runs here, ticking as it cools. The building has a boiler somewhere below.

examineTargets.label: the notice
examineTargets.description: Taped to the wall: MAINTENANCE ONLY — NO ADMITTANCE. The tape is yellowed. No one has read it in years.

rooms.label: Basement Storeroom
rooms.description: Low ceiling, bare concrete. Cardboard boxes, a broken trolley, a mop in a bucket of grey water. A steel door in the far wall opens outward onto the alley — the kind that only unlatches from inside.

addenda.text: The building is moving above you. You can hear feet on the stairs.

exits.label: Out the service door to the alley

examineTargets.label: the cardboard boxes
examineTargets.description: Ministry of Culture letterhead on the side. Pamphlets, most likely. Whatever is inside has not been opened.

examineTargets.label: the service door
examineTargets.description: Steel, well-oiled. A simple latch. From outside there is no handle; from here, it opens easily.

examineTargets.label: the trolley
examineTargets.description: A service trolley with a broken wheel, pushed against the wall. Someone started fixing it and lost interest.

rooms.label: First Floor Landing
rooms.description: Carpeted, quieter than the ground floor. Four numbered doors, all closed. A fire door at the end of the landing connects to the service stairs. The corridor has a different quality of silence to the floor below.

addenda.text: Footsteps from below. Volkov has heard something and is no longer moving slowly.

examineTargets.label: the fire door
examineTargets.description: A heavy fire door at the end of the landing. The service stairs beyond it are used for deliveries and maintenance. The latch opens from this side.

examineTargets.label: the landing window
examineTargets.description: Overlooks the side alley. The grey Peugeot is visible from here — parked, engine off, driver in his seat.

examineTargets.label: the room numbers
examineTargets.description: Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen. Kuznetsov's is the last door. Light under it.

rooms.label: Room 14
rooms.description: A single room — bed, a chair, a small desk. A coat is on the bed, a case beside it, packed. A man in his early fifties sits by the window in the dark. He stands when Jacob enters. The hip is immediately obvious. A walking cane is propped against the windowsill.

addenda.text: Kuznetsov is ready. He has been ready since yesterday.
Voices in the building. Kuznetsov hears them too. His expression does not change.

examineTargets.label: Kuznetsov
examineTargets.description: A lean man with close-cropped grey hair and the careful stillness of someone who has been waiting a long time. He says nothing about the hip. He says nothing at all until you speak.

effect.text: He nods once. He picks up the case. He has been waiting for this moment for two weeks. You help him to his feet.

examineTargets.label: the window
examineTargets.description: The side alley, four floors below. The grey Peugeot is visible — engine off, driver in his seat. He is right where he should be.

examineTargets.label: the case
examineTargets.description: A small leather case, worn at the corners. Whatever is inside, it is not much. He packed light and he packed early.
